title: ר' ירמיה (סתם)

paragraphs: R. Yirmeyah (without further designation), Rav Huna's student, first chapter of Kiddushin [as cited; the discussion is in chapter two, at 45b–46a]. This is an error, for it is R. Yirmeyah bar Abba who is Rav Huna's student. Be'er Sheva, folio 92b, writes that Tosafot in the first chapter of Gittin says there were two R. Yirmeyahs, one in Shemuel's days. He erred, for in the first chapter of Gittin (11b), on 'Rav Huna sat before R. Yirmeyah,' Tosafot writes that there were two Rav Hunas; it does not mention two R. Yirmeyahs. See above, R. Yirmeyah bar Abba: there were two Rav Yirmeyahs. It appears from chapter HaMaddir (75) that he was from Babylonia, for it says, 'One of us, when he goes up there, is worth two of them: R. Yirmeyah, when he was here, did not know what the rabbis were saying, but when he went up there he called us foolish Babylonians.' In Zevaḥim (60b), Pesaḥim (34b), Menaḥot (52a), he said of Rava's words, 'Foolish Babylonians.' They repeated before Rava what R. Yirmeyah had said, 'Foolish Babylonians,' etc. (See Ravin); see above. They expelled him from the study house over his question about one foot within fifty [cubits], first chapter of Bava Batra (it should read chapter Lo Yaḥpor, 23b). At the end of Bava Batra (165b), he said, 'I am unworthy to have you send me this question’ [the cited Bavli reads כדאי where Heilprin has בראי׳], '(but this is your student's opinion).' For this they brought him into the study house. Wherever it says 'They say in the West,' it is R. Yirmeyah, end of chapter 1 of Sanhedrin (17b). He married a priest's daughter. In Shevi'it, chapter 2, halakhah 8, a man gave him a tithe. In chapter Bammeh Ishah (62a): R. Yirmeyah said, 'In the case of a woman who is a treasurer,' etc.; Rabbah bar bar Ḥana said: R. Yoḥanan said, 'You have explained a woman'; rather, Rava said. He asked R. Abba, Shabbat (65a); in Asheri the reading is 'Rav Yehudah asked R. Abba.' He called R. Abba 'master,' provoked him, and appeased him. R. Abba bar Kahana said to him. In bar Mammal's name. He raised an objection against R. Abbahu, who called R. Yirmeyah 'my son,' Bava Metzia (16b). His father-in-law's son shut the door before him; he came before R. Avin and R. Abbahu, Bava Kamma (112a–b; 112b as cited). He said to R. Avin, 'When you go before R. Abbahu, put [the objection] to him,' Keitzad Tzolin (84a). R. Avin called him 'foolish Babylonians' (see his entry). He went behind R. Yirmeyah and sat before R. Yirmeyah. R. Zeira said to him, 'Ask R. Avin, for I explained it to him'—I explained the reason to him, and he agreed with my words—Niddah (42a). His grave is in Tiberias, near the second hot springs of Tiberias, above the first hot springs of Tiberias: R. Yirmeyah's grave is in stone (גא״י [provisionally Gelilot Eretz Yisrael]). In the name of Rav Adda bar Aḥvah. R. Idi of Ḥutrayya said to him. In Ilfa's name, chapter HaMekabbel (114a). And R. Elazar. He asked R. Assi. He spoke to Rav Ashi. R. Bun bar Ḥiyya. Rav Dimi bar Yosef. R. Dostai. Before R. Zeira, Berakhot (30b, before Ein Omedin). He sat before R. Zeira and said to him, 'My teacher, do you say so?' Menaḥot (81, end of side b). He asked R. Zeira, Beitzah (34a), Mo'ed Katan (4a, where R. Zeira called him 'my son'; 12b, 17b), Nedarim (36b), Shabbat (48b), Bekhorot (34b), Zevaḥim (7a, 26a), Gittin (44 [side unspecified]). R. Zeira said: R. Yirmeyah said, Pesaḥim (40a), Shabbat (7a). He hurried to rise for prayer; R. Zeira applied to him, 'He who turns his ear away from hearing Torah,' Shabbat (10a). He sat before him and said, 'What about this?' He said, 'It is forbidden,' there (147a). In Ze'eira's name, and Ze'eira in his name. R. Ze'iri, in his name. He said to R. Zerika, 'When you enter [before] R. Abbahu'; he applied to him, 'Speak truth,' etc. Rav Ḥuna. R. Ḥizkiyah, his student. In R. Ḥiyya the Great's name. In R. Ḥiyya bar Abba's name; he sat before him, beginning of chapter 2 of Berakhot (13b), in שס״ח [provisionally the new Shas], Rif, and Rosh. R. Ḥiyya of Jaffa. He ruled for R. Ḥiyya bar Rav Yitzḥak Atishayya. He asked R. Ḥanina [the cited passage introduces Yirmeyah as the reporter and names Akavya as the questioner], Jerusalem Talmud, Sotah, chapter 4, halakhah 4. R. Ḥanina bar Pappi. R. Ḥanina Antanyya. Ḥanan bar Berekhya of Botzrah, in his name. Rav Ḥisda said (R. Yirmeyah is named in שס״ח, the “new Shas”): Mareimar expounded [compare Gittin 88a, where Ḥisda cites Mar Ukva or, alternatively, Yirmeyah]. Rav Ḥisda bar Yosef asked him (I did not find this). He wrote to R. Yehudah Nesia, Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah, chapter 3, halakhah 2. With R. Yehudah son of R. Simon. He said, 'R. Yoḥanan said,' Yoma (63a; 80, end of side b). In chapter Bammeh Ishah (63b), 'And so R. Yoḥanan said'; Rashi explains: 'I heard from R. Yoḥanan.' R. Yonah. R. Yose bar Avin, in his time. R. Yose Tziyeni asked before him. R. Yasa. R. Yasa, the son of R. Yasa's daughter. He and R. Yaakov called each other 'orphans'—that is, without understanding. R. Yaakov explained it to him. R. Yitzḥak Nappaḥa. Rav Yitzḥak be-Rabbi sat before him. He called R. Yitzḥak bar Yose ‘children’ [in the checked Bavli the plural addresses both Rav Huna and Yitzḥak bar Yosef], Gittin (11b); see his entry. He ruled for R. Yitzḥak Atishayya. R. Yitzḥak bar Redifa. R. Yirmeyah of Difti said. R. Yirmeyah the scribe asked him. R. Yishmael son of R. Tanḥum, his student (I did not find this). In the name of R. Kahana bar Malkya and R. Meyasha the Elder. R. Natan bar Berekhya, his student. Rav Sama son of R. Yirmeyah. In Mar Ukva's name. In Rav's name, Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of chapter Pasin; Horayot (6, end of side a). He called Rava 'foolish Babylonians' (see above). On the day Rava bar Kisa died, he spoke to Rav Ḥisda. Ravin said: R. Yirmeyah said, Yoma (63a). R. Redifa. He said, 'Shemuel said,' Ḥullin (20a), Keitzad Tzolin (76a). R. Shemuel bar Ḥalafta. R. Shemuel, R. Hoshaya's brother, in his name. When R. Shemuel bar Yitzḥak died, R. Yirmeyah asked R. Ze'eira a halakhic question, Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, chapter 3, mishnah 1. R. Yirmeyah spoke in his name, Jerusalem Talmud, Pe'ah, chapter 1, halakhah 1; Eruvin, chapter 1, and beginning of chapter Pasin. Shemuel bar Tanḥum, in his name. In the name of R. Shimon ben Yoḥai, Ḥelek (97b), Sukkah (45b). He said, 'Resh Lakish said.' R. Shimon bar Abba.
